note_add: The site fee includes entry for one vehicle plus one legally towed vehicle or trailer, so a motorhome towing a car pays no extra-vehicle fee; each further vehicle pays a per-night fee at the park, set park by park ($8 at Grover Hot Springs, $10 at Half Moon Bay, Cuyamaca Rancho and Lake Perris). Most campsites take at most two licensed vehicles (14 CCR 4452), a park may set more or fewer. Standard sites take up to eight people; Samuel P. Taylor has cut some sites to six. No per-person charge is published, but no complete fee schedule says there is none. Tax: state law bars any city or county tax on occupying a state park campsite (Rev. & Tax. Code 7282), and California has no state lodging tax. Peak-season, holiday and weekend rates are set park by park, not as a flat premium.

unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Set park by park ($8-10 on the park pages read); only the 'one vehicle plus one towed' rule is statewide.
unsettled.extra_person.amount: Up to 8 people per site, but no source says outright that there is no per-person charge.
unsettled.tax: Rev. & Tax. Code 7282 bars city/county tax on a state park campsite; the state-level zero rests on reading (no state lodging tax), not a quoted source, so no zero is written.

summary: CA: one vehicle plus a towed vehicle included in the site fee (no entrance), extra vehicles a per-park nightly fee, 8 people max, $8.25 reservation fee confirmed, no campsite tax by statute.

note_add: A camper needs no day-use parking permit (display the camping receipt). The permit now costs $10 a day ($12 non-resident) or $60 ($75) for 12 months, replacing the $5 figure above. One car or truck may be towed in free; a second vehicle driven in pays the $10 extra-vehicle fee on site. Eight people a site usually, six at some sites. The overnight-rental rule (OAR 736-015-0020) has no per-person charge for individual sites, only hiker/biker per-person rates. Rates include lodging tax.

If you're camping at a state park, you don't need a day-use parking permit. Just display your current state park camping receipt on your dashboard.
Daily parking permits are $10 per day, per vehicle for residents of Oregon (or $12 per day for non-residents).

A maximum of eight individuals may occupy one campsite unless otherwise specified by the park manager.
OAR 736-015-0020 – Overnight Rentals ... Campsite Rental rates (per night per site before tax)
Oregon Parks and Recreation Department charges out-of-state residents 25% more.

unsettled.extra_person: The zero comes from OAR 736-015-0020: the overnight-rental schedule lists per-site rates and per-person rates only for hiker/biker sites and the group-tent overage. The rates page also lists none.

summary: OR: tax included, campers exempt from day-use permit, $10/night extra vehicle (one towed free), 8 people no per-person charge, $10 reservation fee and 1.25x non-resident confirmed.

note_add: Rule (WAC 352-32-030): one car and one recreational vehicle a site, plus one more vehicle without sleeping quarters where it fits; eight people overnight unless a ranger allows more. The fees page lists no per-person charge.

unsettled.extra_person.amount: Up to 8 people (WAC 352-32-030); the fees page lists no per-person charge but doesn't say it is the complete schedule, so no zero.

summary: WA: tax included, campers need no Discover Pass in their park, $10/night extra vehicle past one, 8 people max; $8/$10 reservation and $15 non-resident per-reservation fees confirmed.

note_add: Correction: one annual pass serves two vehicles, but only one at a time. Bought online, the one-day pass is $11.50 and the annual about $50 with processing fees. Bought at a state park headquarters or from park staff, there is no transaction fee. The one-day pass 'expires the day after the date printed on the pass', so whether one covers an overnight stay is not stated. Not needed at boat-in-only campgrounds.

summary: WA DNR: Discover Pass confirmed as the only charge; restated as $10/vehicle/day with the $45 annual option, and the two-vehicle wording corrected (one vehicle at a time).

note_add: The camping fee is charged per vehicle per night at a per-park figure, so each further vehicle pays the camping fee again. A towed vehicle is free (NAC 407.055(5)), and a site takes at most two motorized vehicles, or one plus a towed vehicle, unless the supervisor allows more. Non-Nevada-registered vehicles pay $5 more per day (NAC 407.055(6)(b)). The posted camping rate is $5 higher for them, and the $10 hook-up fee is the same for everyone. Eight people a site, with no per-person camping charge in the NAC fee schedule (bike-in/walk-in entry is $2 a person). Day-use reservations made before the arrival day carry the same $5 transaction fee; same-day ones carry none.

But the posted camping rate equals the NAC 407.055 entrance plus camping columns (Beaver Dam and Spring Valley $5 + $10 = posted $15; Valley of Fire $10 + $10 = posted $20), and Valley of Fire's group text says 'Camping and day-use fees of $20/vehicle/night'. That strongly suggests the camping rate already includes entry, but no page says so.

unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Equal to each park's per-vehicle camping fee (on the entries).

summary: NV: $5 transaction fee confirmed; non-NV vehicles +$5/night (NAC); camping fee per vehicle, towed free, 2 vehicles and 8 people max with no per-person charge; entrance and tax unsettled.

note_add: The camping fee covers one vehicle for the length of the stay; a second vehicle pays the $7 motor vehicle entry fee per day ($14 for non-residents at Bear Lake, Farragut, Hells Gate, Priest Lake and Round Lake). A vehicle or trailer past the site's maximum pays an $8 overnight fee. IDPR's page gives both figures. The Idaho State Parks Passport ($10 a year with Idaho vehicle registration) covers entry, not camping or extra vehicles. Non-residents pay $3 a night more at most parks; at Farragut, Henrys Lake, Ponderosa, Priest Lake and Round Lake the non-resident campsite fee is $24-80 (Tier A). Eight people a site (16 on a companion site); the campsite fee schedule (IDAPA 26.01.20.250) charges extra people only in cabins and yurts. Posted camping fees include tax. The IDAPA amounts are maximums; the board sets the actual fees.
